Without internet access

Source: vignettes/articles/install-airgapped.Rmd
install-airgapped.Rmd

On a host that cannot reach public registries, the images are brought in by hand: pull and save them on a connected machine, carry the files over, and load them on the host. Then follow the cluster guide with the differences below.

1. The images

These are the images the manifests in k8s-manifests/ use. The automated checks fail if a manifest uses an image that is not listed here.

Image Used by
traefik:v3.5.4 traefik.yml
dexidp/dex:v2.44.0-alpine dex.yml
busybox dex.yml (init container that installs the Dex web theme)
ghcr.io/immunoplex/signup:main@sha256:cd7c59b4e5fb2b5090b6995b96265afcfba6b564a86894c1a2ebbae3a2067a79 dex.yml (signup page; pinned by digest, the image has no release tags)
postgres:17.2 postgresql.yml
ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi:1.3.3 i-spi.yml
ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-api:1.2.0 i-spi-compute.yml, i-spi-compute-sim.yml
ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-worker:1.2.0 i-spi-compute.yml, i-spi-compute-sim.yml
redis:7.4 i-spi-compute.yml, i-spi-compute-sim.yml
traefik/whoami whoami.yml (optional test page)
quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.8.1 whoami.yml (optional test page)

On a connected machine with Docker:

for img in \
  traefik:v3.5.4 \
  dexidp/dex:v2.44.0-alpine \
  busybox \
  ghcr.io/immunoplex/signup:main@sha256:cd7c59b4e5fb2b5090b6995b96265afcfba6b564a86894c1a2ebbae3a2067a79 \
  postgres:17.2 \
  ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi:1.3.3 \
  ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-api:1.2.0 \
  ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-worker:1.2.0 \
  redis:7.4 \
  traefik/whoami \
  quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.8.1
do
  docker pull "$img"
  docker save -o "$(echo "$img" | tr '/:@' '___').tar" "$img"
done

The worker image is about 5 GB; the others together about 3 GB.

2. The cluster’s own images

If the host already runs Kubernetes with cert-manager, skip this step. To build single-node K3s offline, also bring:

  • K3s: the k3s binary, the install script, and the k3s-airgap-images-<arch>.tar.zst bundle for v1.33.5+k3s1. The K3s air-gap documentation describes them.
  • cert-manager v1.19.1: its release manifest (cert-manager.yaml) and the images it names (controller, webhook, cainjector, startupapicheck). Read the exact tags from that manifest, then pull and save them as above.

3. Load the images on the host

Copy every .tar and the .tar.zst bundle to the host, then:

sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/
sudo cp *.tar *.tar.zst /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/

K3s imports everything in that folder when it starts, and within a minute or two when files are added while it runs.

Install K3s without downloading:

sudo cp k3s /usr/local/bin/k3s && sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k3s
INSTALL_K3S_VERSION=v1.33.5+k3s1 INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true ./install.sh --disable=traefik
sudo ln -s /usr/local/bin/kubectl /bin/kubectl

Then continue with step 4 of the cluster guide, applying cert-manager from the copied cert-manager.yaml.

4. Two changes to the manifests

After the sed step of the cluster guide:

  1. Pull policy. dex.yml and postgresql.yml use imagePullPolicy: Always, which tries the registry even when the image is already loaded, and fails offline. Change it:

    sed -i 's/imagePullPolicy: Always/imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent/g' *.yml

  2. The Dex web theme. Dex’s init container downloads its web theme (web.zip) from GitHub on first start. Offline, put the unpacked web/ folder (from templates/web.zip in this repository) on the dex volume at /var/dex/web before starting Dex; the init container then skips the download.

5. Check 

sudo k3s ctr images ls | grep -E 'i-spi|dex|traefik|postgres|signup|redis'

Every image from step 1 should be listed. A pod in ImagePullBackOff almost always means imagePullPolicy: Always on a loaded image, or a tag that differs from the one saved.
